## Setup

Work in your personal `work/session08/` folder. Complete the code chunks below;
they currently contain hints only. Run them in order, then render/knit the file.
If ggplot2 is missing, install it once in the Console with `install.packages("ggplot2")`.

Synthetic data: 40 participants, 20 per arm; one row is one participant.
`change` is `followup - baseline`. This marker has no specified clinical units
or definition of improvement.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(6301)
participant <- data.frame(
  id = sprintf("P%02d", 1:40),
  arm = rep(c("control", "treated"), each = 20),
  baseline = rnorm(40, 5, 1.1)
)
participant$followup <- participant$baseline +
  ifelse(participant$arm == "treated", -0.8, -0.1) + rnorm(40, 0, 0.7)
participant$change <- participant$followup - participant$baseline
table(participant$arm)
```

## Q1. Base R boxplot

Create a **boxplot of `change` by `arm`** using `participant`.

1. Label the x-axis "Randomized arm" and the y-axis "Change in marker (follow-up minus baseline)".
2. Overlay all 40 participant values with horizontal jitter. Keep their vertical values unchanged.
3. Add a dashed horizontal line at zero.

**Answer:** Which arm has the lower median change? What does a negative change mean?

```{r}
# Use outline = FALSE to hide boxplot outlier symbols before adding all points.
# Add stripchart(..., vertical = TRUE, method = "jitter", add = TRUE).
# Add abline(h = 0, lty = 2).
```

## Q2. The same boxplot with ggplot2

1. Add `geom_boxplot()` and horizontally jittered participant points. Display each observation once.
2. Use the same axis labels and dashed zero line as Q1. Add the title "Marker change by randomized arm".
3. Add a caption: "Synthetic data; one point per participant; 20 participants per arm."

**Answer:** Do the two plots tell the same story? What do the points show that the boxes alone do not?

```{r}
# Start with p <- ggplot(participant, aes(x = arm, y = change)) + ...

# Use geom_jitter(width = 0.1, height = 0).
```
